A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, core algorithms and principal context-blind regret bounds. Their main text, equations, pseudocode and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 presents algorithms, theoretical regret bounds and proofs, including Appendix D's mathematical hard instances. It reports no original empirical experiments, simulations or data analyses.

after.justification: v3 remains theoretical throughout. Its context-aware extension and additional appendix lemmas do not include empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: v3 adds Context-AwareBatchLearning (Algorithm 3), which learns its exploration policy from the current batch's observed contexts before choosing actions. v1 learns exploration policies from previous batches and initially uses the local optimal-design policy. The underlying ExplorationPolicy routine is retained; Algorithm 1 also gains the missing regularization term in its first-batch covariance formula.

E1.justification: Neither version actually trains or evaluates on datasets or empirical tasks. The context-aware extension changes the theoretical problem coverage, rather than experimentally tested coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates experimental baselines. Comparisons with Ruan et al. and Zanette et al. concern theoretical guarantees.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an empirical evaluation protocol. Changes to batch schedules and information access concern algorithm design and formal assumptions, not experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests or case studies. Their hard-instance constructions belong to lower-bound proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, error bars or empirical uncertainty estimates. Changes to mathematical concentration inequalities belong to the theory assessment.

E6.justification: Neither version contains numerical experimental results or empirical findings. Added and revised symbolic regret guarantees are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v3 permits history-dependent batch lengths, adds the context-aware definition and matching regret-bound statements, and replaces v1's fixed-schedule lower-bound development in Section 6/Appendix D with the subspace-mixture construction in Section 7. Appendix A revises Pinsker's inequality and adds a time-uniform concentration lemma. The clipping factors in the exploration-policy proof are also corrected. Some new material is defective as printed, including Lemma 18's first tail inequality and unfinished proof passages in Section 4.1.1.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions expand from one batch-learning formulation to optimal tradeoffs for both context-blind and context-aware learning. The original context-blind two-phase guarantee, simpler exploration-policy construction and dynamic matrix-concentration contribution remain.

C2.justification: v3 distinguishes communication/deployment constraints from delayed-reward constraints and explains their different information requirements. Section 3 adds substantive explanations of rare-arm underexploration, the context-blind regret penalty, and why scaled-and-clipped updates improve policy learning. Section 8 explains the advantage of observing current-batch contexts.

D1.justification: The context-aware extension includes explicit pseudocode, context-processing instructions and a batch-length recurrence in Equation 74. Existing regularization and failure-probability choices largely remain. Neither version provides executable code, hardware measurements or a code/data release.

R1.justification: v3 adds Li et al. (2010), removes Yu et al. (2019), and revises the Zanette comparison from the small state-action-space assumption in v1 Section 4.1 to the large-space assumption in v3 Section 3.1. Ruan and Zanette publication updates refer to retained works; the central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively reorganized around two information models. v3 adds a substantial technical overview before the formal analysis, integrates the revised lower-bound development into the main text, relocates the Zanette comparison and adds a conclusion.

P2.justification: v3 switches from A4 to Letter pages, enlarges the text, colors cross-references and reflows equations and algorithm boxes. Algorithm 3 adds a new pseudocode display. The basic single-column presentation remains, with no data figures or tables in either version.

improvement.justification: Relative to v1, v3 provides valuable explanations and broader treatment of information access and adaptive batch schedules. However, new material includes unfinished proofs in Section 4.1.1 and a false first tail inequality in Appendix A, Lemma 18, which fails when all variables are zero. Section 8 also invokes Lemma 7 without resolving its independent-sample requirement when learning and acting on the same contexts. These proof-reliability concerns make the net benefit of the expanded claims uncertain.
